findingRegister.finding: The original and staged example is arithmetically correct, but 246.78 rounded to one decimal place uses a critical digit 8 and produces a tenths digit 8. Those equal digits play different roles. A student copying the critical digit into the answer would get the displayed answer for the wrong reason. Under the campaign numeric-clarity instruction, this worked teaching example should keep the decision digit and resulting digit distinct.

methods.description: Find the requested rounding place, inspect the next digit, keep the rounding digit for 0–4 or increase it for 5–9, and remove later digits. Whole-number rounding, carrying and preserving requested trailing zeros are cases of this method.

Use the critical-digit rule backwards to find the smallest or largest two-decimal-place number giving a stated one-decimal-place result; check the neighbouring hundredth. This is an adaptation of the supplied rounding rule, not an explicitly taught inverse example in the excerpt.
